items.event_time_ist: Wednesday, Oct 21, 2026 (Ushakov post-meeting briefing, St. Petersburg)
items.summary: After a ~3-hour Witkoff-Putin meeting at St. Petersburg's Constantine Palace on Wednesday, Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said Putin agreed 'in principle' that trilateral Russia-US-Ukraine peace talks will continue after Nov 10; future talks to focus on building a post-conflict 'security framework' for Russia and Ukraine. Putin also voiced interest in restoring US-Russia economic cooperation and in a meeting with China to discuss Ukraine (Beijing 'already working on it,' per reports). No sign of movement on Russia's maximalist positions (full Donbas, demilitarization, no NATO); Witkoff delivered the post-Oslo proposal. First time since the row escalated that Moscow has agreed to return to the negotiating table.
items.title: Putin 'in principle' ready to resume trilateral Russia-US-Ukraine talks after Nov 10

items.event_time_ist: Sunday, Oct 18, 2026 (Bloomberg interview published; NBC's Meet the Press aired)
items.summary: In a Sunday Bloomberg interview, Zelensky accused Trump of trying to force Ukraine to surrender: 'I believe steps have been taken to convince Ukraine to capitulate,' adding Trump has 'an instinctive affinity for autocrats.' On NBC's Meet the Press the same day, he said he would run in a wartime presidential election if one took place — the first time he has said so publicly, after months of leaving it open — but played down the prospect: Russia has refused the 60-day ceasefire needed to hold a vote, and a vast majority of Ukrainians oppose wartime elections. He also said the US had suspended intel-sharing for three days (leaving Ukraine without ballistic-missile early warnings) and that Starshield speed limits were still not fully lifted.
items.title: Zelensky says he'd run in a wartime election if one takes place — first time publicly (catch-up, Oct 18)
